title: A structurally malformed save can erase the live run while reporting success
evidence: Controlled corruption fixture: node.path=[[1]] passes _validate_save. load_game returns true and 'Game loaded.' after _apply_save raises an index error and leaves only node 1. Evidence: probes/corrupt_save.log; simulation_project/corrupt_save_results.json.
reproduction: In an isolated copy, save a valid two-node run, replace a path point with [1], then Load. Related unvalidated required tunnel/packet/contract fields also pass the validator.
impact: Loading a parseable but damaged save changes live state before failure; the success message conceals lost structures.
recommendation: Validate every field and nested collection that _apply_save or simulation consumes; build a complete temporary restored state and commit it only after all coercion and invariants succeed.
acceptance: Malformed vector paths, missing required fields and wrong collection types are refused; the existing run remains byte-equivalent and Load returns false.

title: Save validation accepts cycles, duplicate identities and unknown tunnel definitions
evidence: Controlled schema fixtures all return an empty validation error for hub→child→hub cycles, duplicate node.id and a connected node.tunnel='invalid'. Runtime consequences follow unchecked recursion/dictionary access in _calc_subtree and upkeep. Evidence: simulation_results save_cycle/save_duplicate_id/save_unknown_tunnel.
reproduction: Mutate a valid serialized fixture's parent graph, node IDs or tunnel key; call _validate_save. These are synthetic damaged saves, not a legal-play topology.
impact: An accepted save can overwrite the hub, recurse indefinitely, or fail the first simulation tick.
recommendation: Require unique matching node IDs/keys, one root hub, valid parents, acyclic parent chains, valid tunnel/path state for every link, and valid packet-route references.
acceptance: Each invalid graph is rejected without applying it; a valid disconnected branch remains loadable.

title: Loaded numeric values lack bounds and can overwrite nodes or create invalid camera state
evidence: A fixture with next_id=1, camera zoom=0 and compute=-100 is accepted with no validation error; _apply_save assigns these values directly. Evidence: simulation_results save_invalid_ranges.
reproduction: Edit these numeric fields in a valid isolated save and validate it. Other bounded fields include size, cap_rate, lane, accumulator and quarantine/boost timers.
impact: The next placement can reuse the hub ID; invalid zoom and negative or extreme simulation values enter a supposedly validated run.
recommendation: Validate finite numeric values and their allowed ranges, require next_id greater than every restored ID, and validate footprint bounds and sizes.
acceptance: Reject nonfinite/out-of-range values and colliding next_id while preserving the current run; all saves generated by normal play pass.

title: Save version and researched IDs are trusted without compatibility checks
evidence: Validator accepts version='999.0' and researched=['invalid_tech']; _is_unlocked later indexes TECH[t] without a guard. Evidence: simulation_results save_unknown_version/save_unknown_research.
reproduction: Validate a current save with an unknown version or researched ID. This is a controlled forward-version/damaged-save fixture.
impact: Unsupported saves appear to load successfully and can fail when tool availability is queried.
recommendation: Declare supported save schema versions, migrate known older versions and reject incompatible ones; validate researched IDs or explicitly ignore unknown optional entries.
acceptance: A future schema produces a clear compatibility message; unknown research never causes a dictionary access error; supported older saves migrate correctly.

title: Saving over a parseable invalid file destroys the last-good backup
evidence: Controlled file fixture: create two valid saves, replace current save with {"version":"0.6.4"}, then Save. _read_valid_save(backup) changes from non-null to null. Rotation checks only JSON dictionary parsing, not _validate_save. Evidence: simulation_results invalid_backup_rotation.
reproduction: Use isolated save paths; create a valid backup, corrupt current save with valid JSON lacking game state, then save the active run.
impact: The only recoverable previous run is replaced by semantically unusable data, so a later failed/corrupt current save has no recovery path.
recommendation: Rotate the current file only when the same full validator used for loading accepts it; preserve the previous backup otherwise.
acceptance: After saving over parseable invalid JSON, the previous backup remains valid and unchanged; ordinary valid rotation still works.

title: Save rotation ignores copy and deletion failures before removing the current file
evidence: save_game removes an existing backup, ignores the return from copy_absolute, removes the current save, then attempts rename_absolute. Only the final rename is checked. No OS I/O-failure injection was performed.
reproduction: Source review; relevant situations are a locked file, denied backup write or a filesystem error during rotation.
impact: A failed backup copy can discard both the old backup and current save before the new file is installed.
recommendation: Check each filesystem result, preserve at least one valid old file until replacement succeeds, and report the failed stage. Use a checked replace/rename strategy appropriate to the platform.
acceptance: Injected copy/replace failures return false and leave a valid loadable current or backup file; success is reported only after final replacement is readable.

title: Save/load changes node iteration order and therefore deterministic threat selection
evidence: Controlled valid roundtrip: nodes inserted [1,2,10], equal-depth sweep targets2 before save; JSON.stringify sorts object keys, load rebuilds nodes [1,10,2], next sweep targets10. RNG restoration alone does not preserve behavior. Evidence: simulation_results saved_iteration_order.
reproduction: Compare _launch_sweep before and after a JSON save/load roundtrip of two equally deep branches with IDs2 and10.
impact: Continuing changes target tie-breaking and the order in which random packet-loss draws are assigned to producers.
recommendation: Use stable numeric node ordering in order-sensitive simulation loops or serialize/restore explicit ordering; specify deterministic sweep tie-breaking.
acceptance: Identical state plus identical RNG resumes the same packet-loss assignments and next sweep target across save/load.

title: Outbound processor-input packets can follow an obsolete rerouted chain
evidence: Controlled topology fixture: C2→node2→Forge3 input route[2,3]; reroute Forge3 to C2 while packet is on edge2. Packet survives with idx=1, route[2,3] although Forge3.parent=1. Stale-hop check only checks dir==1. Evidence: simulation_results stale_downward_route.
reproduction: Start a conversion input travelling outward, dismantle/reroute the downstream processor link before input reaches the junction, then let it cross the next hop.
impact: Input can jump onto a link whose live start is elsewhere, producing resources through a physically impossible route.
recommendation: Validate adjacency in both directions and invalidate packets whenever any stored edge's endpoints no longer match the route snapshot.
acceptance: Upbound and downbound packets are canceled on changed route adjacency; unchanged packets still arrive exactly once.

title: Delivery contracts count net wallet changes, allowing refunds to satisfy deliveries
evidence: Legal-placement path with a controlled valid Cycles20 offer: place two valid Mirai, accept at60 Cycles, undo both, job completes with progress20 and packets_delivered=0. A separate controlled Intel fixture records20 delivered then spends5: progress15, not20. Evidence: simulation_results legal_placement_refund_contract/consumed_deliveries_contract.
reproduction: Accept a Cycles delivery job after spending20 on undoable buildings; undo them. Alternatively deliver required Intel while a Market/Lab consumes some before completion.
impact: Rewards can be earned without delivery, while productive consumption prevents real deliveries from satisfying the advertised objective.
recommendation: Track per-resource cumulative C2 deliveries and snapshot that counter on acceptance; exclude refunds and emergency grants. If retained stock is intentional, rename the objective and still exclude refunds explicitly.
acceptance: Refunding buildings does not advance delivery progress;20 genuine delivered units complete a20-unit job even when subsequently consumed.

title: Fuel-starved processors still contribute full traffic and overload other branches
evidence: Controlled Forge fixture has100 Intel,0 Cycles: _node_traffic reports1.2 packets/s, but a simulation tick spawns0 processor input packets. Traffic predicate checks input only; production also requires fuel. Evidence: simulation_results converter_no_fuel.
reproduction: Run a connected Forge/Lab with stocked Intel but insufficient Cycles; inspect offered subtree traffic on a shared trunk.
impact: Nonexistent work adds overload loss to genuine producers and gives misleading bottleneck diagnostics.
recommendation: Use the same operational/input/fuel predicate for offered processor traffic and actual conversion scheduling, or derive load from real emitted traffic.
acceptance: A processor unable to afford fuel injects0 offered conversion load and cannot make a shared trunk appear overloaded.

title: Advertised capacity behaves as a soft loss parameter rather than a throughput ceiling
evidence: Measured controlled fixture: DNS cap3, offered4, distance loss0.03 produces modeled delivered3.2133/s. At extreme overload the0.9 loss ceiling lets arbitrarily large offered load exceed capacity. This is an observed model choice, not a proven design-intent bug. Evidence: simulation_results capacity_soft_ceiling.
reproduction: Compare _edge.cap and _edge.delivered on an overloaded DNS trunk. Prior acceptance checks did not require a hard cap.
impact: Players cannot infer what a3-packet/s link can actually carry; node throughput ceilings cease to be ceilings.
recommendation: Either enforce an actual delivery/admission ceiling with queue/drop behavior, or explicitly call the displayed value a soft bandwidth/loss rating and teach that model.
acceptance: For a hard-cap design, sustained delivery never exceeds declared capacity; for a soft model, inspector and help text clearly state the nonlinear rule.

title: A connected Cycles producer at zero output suppresses emergency recovery
evidence: Controlled connected Mirai fixture with cap_rate=0 and compute=0 reports production{compute:0}, has_income=true, reserve=false and compute remains0. _has_cycle_income checks type/on but not effective production. Evidence: simulation_results zero_output_emergency.
reproduction: Set the output limit of the only connected Cycles producer to0%, deplete Cycles and tick the simulation.
impact: The emergency reserve's stated no-income condition is false despite zero production, and paid rebuilding actions remain blocked.
recommendation: Test effective positive Cycles production when deciding whether emergency supply is unnecessary; explain the zero-output reason when a manual setting disables income.
acceptance: At0% effective output and no other Cycles income, the reserve reaches the intended bootstrap floor; restoring positive production ends reserve behavior correctly.

title: Disabling a forwarding structure silences its live tunnel without stopping transit
evidence: Controlled trunk fixture: disabled node2 still has operational TCP path and forwards an enabled Phishing child; upkeep0.5 remains charged, but trace10 decays to9.88 with no TCP noise. Noise predicate requires source-node on, unlike forwarding. Evidence: simulation_results disabled_tunnel_noise.
reproduction: Place a producer/forwarder on a loud trunk, connect active child producers through it, then Disable the trunk's source structure.
impact: A functioning loud tunnel becomes free of noise merely by disabling unrelated local production; this undermines protocol/counterplay choices.
recommendation: Define noise by active tunnel/transit state rather than local producer on/off; if quiet empty links are intended, distinguish idle from actively forwarding.
acceptance: A disabled local producer forwarding packets through TCP still contributes the documented TCP noise; truly inactive links follow an explicit quiet rule.

title: A footprint can enter a guarded district while paying the unguarded origin's breach cost
evidence: Controlled vision-position fixture on generated seed12345: Fence origin(75,9) hasICE0, center(76,10) hasICE1; placement succeeds and pays0 Tools. Both validation/payment use origin while ownership uses center elsewhere. Evidence: simulation_results footprint_ice_bypass.
reproduction: Place a2×2 structure across a district boundary with its origin on unguarded ground and center in a guarded district. Fixture moved C2 only to isolate reachability; not presented as a completed legal expansion.
impact: Border positioning bypasses security costs for a structure owned by guarded territory.
recommendation: Choose one ownership/security anchor consistently for display, validation and payment, or charge the maximum ICE of occupied districts if that is the intended rule.
acceptance: Every boundary orientation charges the agreed district/security rule, including affordability checks and exact Undo refund.

title: Mirai consumes shared Cycles district slots but bypasses their placement limit
evidence: Controlled district fixture with Registry cap2 legally passes _placement_error for3 spaced Mirai; _slots_left then returns-1. Mirai is counted by _slots_left but its placement branch omits the limit. Evidence: simulation_results nest_slot_bypass.
reproduction: Fill a Cycles district using Mirai. This probe uses a controlled2-slot district to isolate the rule, not a naturally generated whole-map district.
impact: The same district-capacity indicator applies inconsistently and can show negative slots; Mirai can occupy beyond the cap while other Cycles payloads are blocked.
recommendation: Apply the same capacity rule to all slot-consuming Cycles producers, or explicitly exempt Mirai from both occupancy counting and the displayed limit.
acceptance: No producer counted toward slots can make slots negative; exempt types are consistently excluded from both counting and validation.

title: DDoS is advertised as quarantine recovery but leaves quarantine timers unchanged
evidence: Controlled fixture: successful40-Cycle/1-Tool scrub sets trace0 but leaves quarantine5 unchanged. Inspector explicitly says 'wait it out or DDoS' for quarantine. Evidence: simulation_results scrub_retains_quarantine.
reproduction: Use DDoS after a sweep has already quarantined a host; observe its remaining quarantine and connectivity.
impact: Players spend scarce Tools expecting immediate branch recovery that the action does not perform.
recommendation: Choose the rule explicitly: clear quarantine on successful DDoS if it is a recovery action, or change inspector/action copy to say it only stops future tracing and current quarantine must expire.
acceptance: Action results match its preview and inspector guidance; quarantine recovery or retained timers are unambiguous.

title: Overclock charges full cost on disabled or unreachable producers
evidence: Controlled fixtures: disabled Mirai and disconnected Mirai both spend20 Cycles and receive boost_t20; disabled production is{}, disconnected chain is[]. Evidence: simulation_results disabled_overclock/offline_overclock.
reproduction: Select a disabled or offline producer and press Overclock; the timer runs while it cannot deliver additional production.
impact: A contextual action consumes scarce starting resources despite no current benefit, with no confirmation of a queued strategy.
recommendation: Gate the command on operational positive-output state or explicitly offer a queued boost that begins when the host is online. Show the reason when unavailable.
acceptance: Disabled/offline/0%-output targets cannot silently spend20 Cycles on an expiring unusable boost; operational targets retain the existing behavior.

title: Unlimited-time full Undo refunds allow temporary production infrastructure at no capital cost
evidence: Source confirms place/tunnel Undo refunds complete cost and has no elapsed-time or produced-output condition; production earnings are retained. Undo stack is limited by20 actions, not time. No abuse playthrough is claimed.
reproduction: Build a small producer and tunnel, allow it to earn while making no new undoable actions, then Undo both.
impact: Full construction refunds undermine investment tradeoffs and can make temporary infrastructure economically free.
recommendation: Playtest a short full-refund grace period, followed by explicit salvage value, while retaining easy correction of immediate placement mistakes.
acceptance: Immediate accidental placement remains reversible at full cost; established earning infrastructure follows a clearly shown salvage policy.

title: Market saturation immediately reverses when the player spends Cash
evidence: Measured controlled wallet fixture: at1000 Cash quote0.50; spending500 Cash raises quote0.75 without a change in sales volume. _market_price depends solely on present resources.credits. Evidence: simulation_results wallet_market_price.
reproduction: Compare sale quote before and after buying Cash-costing infrastructure.
impact: The description says sales saturate demand, but buying upgrades restores demand instantly; the intended diversification incentive is weak and hard to understand.
recommendation: Choose wallet-sensitive pricing deliberately and explain it, or base saturation on cumulative/recent sales with an explicit recovery mechanism.
acceptance: A spending-only action has the documented pricing effect; market-demand changes can be explained from visible inputs.

title: Disabling a processor has no explicit policy for already travelling inputs
evidence: Controlled in-flight fixture: send Intel toward Forge, Disable Forge before arrival, then advance packets; Tools still increases1 although on=false. Inputs/fuel are paid at dispatch, so completing queued work may be intentional. Evidence: simulation_results disabled_inflight_converter.
reproduction: Disable a Forge/Lab/Mixer while its input packet is travelling from C2.
impact: 'Disabled' leaves players unsure whether production stops immediately or accepted work finishes; hidden queued work complicates resource planning.
recommendation: Specify finish-queued-work or immediate-stop behavior. If finishing work, show pending conversions and 'stopping after current inputs'; if stopping immediately, define input/fuel refund or loss.
acceptance: Inspector and action text explain the chosen pending-work policy; input and fuel accounting remain conserved under Disable, removal and reroute.
